items.title: A Second Kind of Grasping: Familiar Objects, Four Driving Forces, and Why Grasping Itself Isn't Always the Problem

items.zh: 復有餘類執取其相、執取隨好。言取相者，謂色境界在可見處，能生作意正現在前，眼見眾色。如是名為執取其相。取隨好者，謂即色境在可見處，能生作意正現在前，眼見色已；然彼先時從他聞有如是如是眼所識色，即隨所聞名句文身，為其增上為依為住，如是士夫補特伽羅，隨其所聞，種種分別眼所識色。如是名為執取隨好。如於其眼所識色中，如是於耳鼻舌身意所識法中，當知亦爾。又此取相及取隨好，或有由此因緣、由此依處、由此增上，發生種種惡不善法，令心流漏；或有由此因緣、由此依處、由此增上，不生種種惡不善法，令心流漏。若於此中執取其相，執取隨好，不如正理，由此因緣、由此依處、由此增上，發生種種惡不善法，令心流漏。彼於如是色類境界，遠離取相及取隨好。云何名為惡不善法？謂諸貪欲，及貪所起諸身惡行、諸語惡行、諸意惡行；若諸瞋恚、若諸愚癡，及二所起諸身惡行、諸語惡行、諸意惡行。是名種種惡不善法。
items.en: There is, further, a second kind that grasps the general mark and grasps the alluring details. Grasping the general mark means that a visible object is present within sight, the attention able to give rise [to eye-consciousness] is directly engaged, and the eye sees the many forms present. …Grasping the alluring details means that, this visible object being present within sight … resting on, taking as its basis, whatever names, phrases, and syllables were previously heard about it, such a person, in accordance with what was heard, variously discriminates the form known by the eye. …This grasping of the general mark and the alluring details may, through this cause, this basis, this governing condition, give rise to various unwholesome states, letting the mind leak out into affliction; or it may, through this same cause, basis, and governing condition, not give rise to any unwholesome states at all. …It is craving, and the bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct arising from craving; it is hatred, and it is delusion, together with the bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct arising from these two. This is called various unwholesome states.

items.zh: 云何由彼令心流漏？謂若於彼彼所緣境界，心、意、識生，遊行流散；即於彼彼所緣境界，與心、意、識種種相應，能起所有身語惡行貪瞋癡生，遊行流散。是名由彼令心流漏。如是於眼所識色中，乃至於意所識法中，執取其相及取隨好，由是發生種種雜染。彼於取相及取隨好能遠離故，便不發生種種雜染。若由忘念，或由煩惱極熾盛故，雖獨閑居，由先所見眼所識色增上力故，或先所受耳鼻舌身意所識法增上力故，發生種種惡不善法，隨所發生而不執著，尋便斷滅、除棄、變吐，是名於彼修行律儀。

items.title: Knowing What to Look At and What Not To: Old Age and Sickness Versus Entertainment

items.zh: 若於其眼所識色中，應策眼根；及於其耳鼻舌身意所識法中，應策意根；即便於彼作意策發。如是策發，令不雜染。由是因緣，於此雜染防護眼根，廣說乃至防護意根；如是名為防護眼根，廣說乃至防護意根。若於其眼所識色中，不應策發所有眼根，及於其耳鼻舌身意所識法中，不應策發所有意根；即便於彼遍一切種而不策發。不策發故，令不雜染。由是因緣，於此雜染修根律儀。如是名為能正修行眼根律儀，廣說乃至能正修行意根律儀。如是應知已廣分別根
items.en: Regarding forms known by the eye, where the eye faculty should be roused … one applies attention and rouses it accordingly there. Rousing it in this way, one keeps the mind free of defilement. …Regarding forms known by the eye, where the eye faculty should not be roused … one, in every such case, does not rouse it at all. By not rousing it, one keeps the mind free of defilement. …[The commentarial gloss (披尋記) explains:] As for the kind of forms one should observe: bodies aged, decrepit, frail, short of breath; bodies bent, leaning on a staff, trembling; or bodies afflicted with serious illness — and so on at length. As for forms the eye faculty should not be roused towards: the kind one should not observe, such as courtesans' entertainment, laughter and revelry, or other performances of song and dance and music — and so on at length.

items.zh: 律儀相。云何當知此中略義？

items.title: A Five-Part Summary: Who Protects, What Is Protected, From What, and How

items.zh: 此略義者，謂若能防護、若所防護、若從防護、若如防護、若正防護。如是一切，總略為一，名根律儀。今於此中誰能防護？謂防守正念，及所修習常委正念，是能防護。何所防護？謂防護眼根，防護耳鼻舌身意根，是所防護。從何防護？謂從可愛、不可愛色，廣說乃至從其可愛、不可愛法而正防護。如何防護？謂不取相、不取隨好。若依是處發生種種惡不善法，令心流漏，即於此處修行律儀。防守根故，名修律儀。如是防護。
items.en: This summary meaning is: who protects; what is protected; from what one protects; how one protects; and correct protection itself. All of this together, in brief, is called restraint of the faculties. …It is guarding mindfulness and the sustained mindfulness cultivated from it — this is who protects. …It is guarding the eye faculty, guarding the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind faculties — this is what is protected. …It is from agreeable and disagreeable forms, and so on at length, from agreeable and disagreeable mental objects, that one correctly protects — this is from what one protects. …It is not grasping the general mark, not grasping the alluring details; and, should various unwholesome states nonetheless arise in dependence on these, letting the mind leak into affliction, then practising restraint precisely there — guarding the faculty in this way is called practising restraint. This is how one protects.

blocks.text: A second kind of grasping, driven not by what is in front of the eyes but by memory and hearsay. One passage (0407b12) is untranslated; it is summarised below.

Grasping can happen when an object is present ("the eye sees the many forms") or "resting on whatever names, phrases, and syllables were previously heard about it". Master Cháng Bǎi: four forces drive it: desire, memory, the force of the object itself, and past habit. Grasping the mark is not itself a fault, he adds, but one must discern.

"Leaking" means that consciousness flows out towards objects and, with them, gives rise to greed, hatred, delusion, and misconduct. Not grasping the mark and details, one prevents this. And if, through forgetfulness or strong affliction, an unwholesome state arises even in solitude, from the memory of something seen or heard before, one does not hold on to it, but "immediately cuts it off, casts it away, spits it out". That is restraint.

One should look at what purifies the mind: old age, sickness, death, the impermanence of things. One should not look at what defiles: entertainments, dances, displays. Venerable Miào Jìng: "one principle: if it makes the mind pure, do it; if it makes the mind impure, don't."

Who protects (mindfulness, and sustained mindfulness); what is protected (the senses); from what (agreeable and disagreeable objects); how (not grasping marks or details); and correct protection itself. Venerable Miào Jìng: it means halting the false discrimination of things as agreeable or disagreeable.

quiz.q: In the second kind, on what basis does one grasp the alluring details of a form?
options: the names, phrases, and syllables previously heard, discriminating in line with what was heard
someone pointing it out on the spot
quiz.why: "Resting on, taking as its basis, whatever names, phrases, and syllables were previously heard about it, such a person, in accordance with what was heard, variously discriminates the form known by the eye." Venerable Miào Jìng: those who have read much discriminate much; those who have read little discriminate little.

quiz.q: Which four forces does Master Cháng Bǎi say drive the sixth consciousness to grasp marks?
options: desire, memory, the force of the object, and past habit
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it is influenced by four forces — desire, memory, the force of the object, and past habit.

quiz.q: The text says grasping may or may not give rise to unwholesome states. How do the masters view grasping itself?
options: both say grasping is always a fault
Cháng Bǎi: grasping itself is not a fault but needs discernment; Miào Jìng: a Buddhist who attends wisely may grasp yet not give rise to unwholesome states
both say to close the eyes
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: grasping the mark and details is not in itself a fault, but one must discern. Venerable Miào Jìng: here it differs — this is a Buddhist who attends wisely; though they too grasp mark and details, no unwholesome states follow.

quiz.q: When one rouses the eye faculty where it should be roused, what is the result?
options: the mind is kept free of defilement
quiz.why: "Rousing it in this way, one keeps the mind free of defilement." Venerable Miào Jìng: if an object helps purify the mind, one should rouse the eye to look at it.

quiz.q: What principle does Venerable Miào Jìng give for deciding whether to rouse the eye?
options: if it is not defiling and makes the mind pure, do it
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: one principle — if it is not defiling and makes the mind pure, you should do it. Whatever makes the mind impure, do not engage the faculties with it.

quiz.q: Into which five items does the treatise summarise restraint of the faculties?
options: discipline, concentration, wisdom, liberation, knowledge of liberation
who protects, what is protected, from what, how, and correct protection
quiz.why: "This summary meaning is: who protects; what is protected; from what one protects; how one protects; and correct protection itself." Master Cháng Bǎi explains each in turn.

quiz.q: "From what one protects" is agreeable and disagreeable objects. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say one actually does?
options: stop the false discrimination of agreeable and disagreeable
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: it means bringing to a halt the false discrimination of things as agreeable or disagreeable.
